renderEvidence.reviewPrinciple: A release-relevant premium-art failure visible at actual card scale is sufficient for REWORK; larger detail inspection is not required to reject that exact hash. Replacement hashes require fresh card/detail review.

familyFindings.companions: All 12 are recognizable, distinct and child-friendly, but the actual Store pixels consistently read as flat centered vector mascots with limited three-quarter anatomy, material response, cast/rim lighting and tier progression. Identity/originality are not the problem; premium dimensional collectible execution is.
familyFindings.beds: All 12 are readable and varied, but the actual Store pixels remain predominantly frontal flat furniture icons. Mattress/frame/canopy/loft/pod construction, material depth and tier spectacle are insufficient relative to the dimensional screenshot contract.

reviews.name: Sprout Pup
reviews.reason: The selected/detail pixels show a cute, readable Sprout Pup, but it is essentially a flat centered mascot with minimal head/body depth, plush/fur material or three-quarter toy lighting. Preserve the friendly starter identity while giving it dimensional anatomy and soft collectible materials.

reviews.name: Moon Cat
reviews.reason: Cat/moon/pixel identity reads clearly, but the actual card is a dark frontal vector mascot with little body volume or material lighting. Keep Tier 1 simple while adding dimensional toy-cat anatomy, surface response and controlled moon/pixel light.

reviews.name: Berry Bunny
reviews.reason: Bunny and berry cues are immediately legible, but the symmetric face/body and berry detail read as flat graphics. Add plush/fur volume, ear/body depth and soft three-quarter lighting while retaining the clean starter silhouette.

reviews.name: Sunny Bird
reviews.reason: The cheerful bird identity is clear, but the body/wings are simple flat shapes with little feather/toy material or spatial depth. Give the bird rounded collectible anatomy, layered wings and garden-lit dimensional shading.

reviews.name: Pebble Turtle
reviews.reason: The low turtle silhouette and shell are distinct, but the side-on card lacks convincing shell curvature, body volume and Galaxy Glow material. Add sculpted shell/body depth, pebble texture and subtle luminous treatment.

reviews.name: Comet Fox
reviews.reason: Fox/star identity is recognizable, but the centered mascot anatomy remains shallow and graphic. Add real muzzle/torso/limb/tail depth, plush-toy material and directional comet/sun lighting without changing the friendly expression.

reviews.name: Story Owl
reviews.reason: Owl and story/book cues are distinct, but the locked Store card still reads as flat layered circles/wings with limited feather or toy volume. Tier 3 needs stronger sculpted anatomy, material separation and Aqua Wave lighting.

reviews.name: Bubble Axolotl
reviews.reason: External gills make the axolotl identifiable, but the image is a flat symmetric sticker-like mascot and the bubble treatment lacks translucent depth. Add rounded aquatic anatomy, refractive bubbles and dimensional Art Attack accents.

reviews.name: Garden Snail
reviews.reason: The side-profile snail/spiral is readable, but shell/body and garden details remain mostly planar. Add volumetric shell gloss, soft body depth, layered botanical detail and controlled Star Luxe highlights appropriate to Tier 3.

reviews.name: Pixel Bot
reviews.reason: Robot identity and neon screen cues are clear, but the Tier-4 card still resembles a flat vector mascot. Increase hardware/panel depth, joints, metallic material response, emissive screen/neon light and three-quarter stance.

reviews.name: Dream Dragon
reviews.reason: Dragon silhouette, wings and pastel direction are readable, but the anatomy and wing layers are flattened and lack Tier-4 material richness. Add sculpted head/body/wing depth, soft candy materials and controlled dream glow.

reviews.name: Star Unicorn
reviews.reason: The high-tier unicorn is unmistakable, but it remains a mostly flat white/pastel mascot with limited horn, mane, body and lighting depth. Tier 5 needs a clearly premium sculpted collectible pose, luxe materials and stronger star/adventure spectacle.

reviews.name: Starter Bed
reviews.reason: Readable starter-bed identity, but the selected/detail and grid pixels remain a flat front-facing furniture icon with little mattress/frame depth, believable material response or three-quarter collectible lighting. Rebuild the same simple starter concept with clear mattress thickness, frame perspective and soft dimensional light.

reviews.name: Cloud Bed
reviews.reason: Cloud styling is recognizable, but the bed reads as a flat frontal icon. Galaxy Glow is mostly palette/motif rather than luminous material; add true bed depth, plush cloud volume and restrained galaxy lighting while keeping Tier 1 simple.

reviews.name: Pixel Bunk
reviews.reason: Pixel cues are visible, but the bunk construction is not convincingly dimensional at card scale and the Sunny Pop identity is secondary to flat block shapes. Clarify stacked-bed/ladder depth and use dimensional sunny materials without overloading Tier 1.

reviews.name: Berry Daybed
reviews.reason: The berry/daybed direction is readable, but the silhouette remains front-flat and does not convincingly show chaise/daybed depth, upholstery or Aqua Wave material. Add side depth, layered cushion/bolster construction and controlled aqua highlights.

reviews.name: Garden Canopy
reviews.reason: Canopy/garden cues exist, but posts, drape/foliage and bed volume collapse into a flat card icon; Art Attack is weak. Rebuild with visible canopy depth, layered fabric/foliage and dimensional art-theme detailing.

reviews.name: Galaxy Gamer Bed
reviews.reason: Gamer/space cues distinguish the item, but the furniture remains a shallow frontal block with little tech hardware, bedding depth or Star Luxe material response. Add believable 3D bed/tech construction and richer but controlled luminous surfaces.

reviews.name: Sunny Loft Bed
reviews.reason: Loft identity is not strong enough through the real locked-card treatment; the structure reads flat and Midnight Neon relies on color rather than luminous architecture. Clarify loft height, ladder/platform depth and neon edge lighting for Tier 3.

reviews.name: Aqua Bubble Bed
reviews.reason: Bubble/aqua motifs are visible, but the bed body is still a flat frontal icon and Candy Core is not materially expressed. Add translucent bubble volume, plush candy material and three-quarter bed geometry without sacrificing card readability.

reviews.name: Art Studio Bed
reviews.reason: The current card does not separate the Art Studio concept strongly enough from a decorated generic bed. Add real studio function—integrated storage/tools/work surface—and three-quarter furniture depth while preserving the Adventure Club theme.

reviews.name: Neon Pod Bed
reviews.reason: Pod/neon direction is present, but the enclosure does not read as a convincing volumetric pod and Tier 4 spectacle is mostly flat glow. Build a clear cocoon shell, inset mattress depth, cloud-soft materials and controlled neon rim/bloom.

reviews.name: Dream Princess Loft
reviews.reason: Princess/loft cues read, but the architecture remains a flat furniture emblem. Tier 4 needs layered loft structure, steps/rails/canopy depth, richer material hierarchy and intentional Pixel Party accents rather than surface decoration.

reviews.name: Luxe Star Canopy
reviews.reason: Star/canopy identity is clear, but the highest tier is still a symmetric flat icon with insufficient drape, frame, textile and metallic depth. Rebuild as a premium three-quarter hero canopy with layered fabric, luxe trim, rich berry lighting and spectacular but readable star detail.
